Owner standing rule #9: ALL kernel perf tuning belongs to compile.py — every perf-shaped constant becomes a registered SG_TUNED_* dim; hand-tuning is banned. Your deliverable: the complete codebase-wide registration plan. Edit NOTHING (a sibling is editing compile.py); your final message is the plan.

SWEEP (every file): grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/*.cuh + gfx942/*.hip.hpp (block sizes, unroll factors, vec widths, smem usage); csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cuh+.cu (256 thr/CTA, SG2_MEGA_BLOCK, samples-per-CTA loops, recompute-vs-cache, barrier variant, reduction granularity, queue strategy); the new wgmma.cuh + tile_pipeline.cuh template params; csrc/backends/pallas/*.py (block sizes, grid tiles); csrc/scan; csrc/algorithms (math headers — should be NONE; flag any).

For EACH constant: file:line, current value, proposed dim name (SG_TUNED_*), candidate values + why, SAFE/RISKY (RISKY = affects determinism/parity, e.g. reduction order or smem layout → needs gate re-run after sweep), kernel-consumption status (#ifdef exists yes/no), which compile.py builder registers it (read _sm90_full_space ~L1763, _gfx942_full_space ~L1857, _pallas_common_dims; the cost-model list ~L4357 + _DEAD_KEY_DIMS ~L1350 + megakernel_cell_search_space ~L2158 — register a dim → 5-spot recipe from the reviews). Distinguish structural (variant-style dims: GEMM_IMPL/BARRIER/DW_SCHEME/SAMPLES_PER_CTA — both code paths must exist) vs numeric. Exclude: Python orchestration timeouts, race hyperparams (Optuna territory), shape/math constants. Order: existing kernels NOW vs R2-headers later. Estimate sweep cost per arch. RIGOR: cite everything; honest SAFE/RISKY; no aspiration.

1	# Autotuner → Product-Build Linkage (operator runbook)
2	
3	**What this covers.** How to make `compile.py`'s autotuned launch parameters
4	ACTIVE in the shipped `grokking_optimizers/_ops*.so` — produce winners, rebuild
5	so the per-TU flags are baked in, verify they actually landed, and re-run the
6	parity + roofline gates against the tuned binary.
7	
8	**Background — lever (b).** The `compile.py` JIT autotuner builds and times
9	kernel variants and picks a winner per `(optimizer, model, arch)`. Historically
10	that winner only reached a header that nothing on the install path included, so
11	the product `.so` shipped the in-header defaults — the autotuner was
12	decorative. The linkage now is:
13	
14	```
15	compile.py build_jit  --(write-on-win, atomic)-->  grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json
16	                                                          |
17	pip install -e .  /  ./build.sh                           v
18	   setup.py TunedBuildExtension  --reads JSON, injects per-TU nvcc flags-->  _ops*.so
19	```
20	
21	The five SAFE per-TU dims are applied: `-DSG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE`,
22	`-DSG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH`, `-DSG_TUNED_UNROLL`, `-DSG_TUNED_ASYNC_DEPTH`, and
23	`--maxrregcount=N` (only when N>0). They go onto each optimizer's CUDA TUs
24	(`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/launch_<opt>.cu` and the megakernel cells
25	`csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu`). The per-optimizer kernel header
26	`kernels/sm_90/<opt>_sm90.cuh` is `#include`d by `launch_<opt>.cu`, so flags on
27	the launcher TU reach the kernel body. Bindings (`*.cpp`), model-only TUs
28	(`models/<model>.cu`), and common/header TUs get **no** per-optimizer flags and
29	keep their in-header defaults. (`cluster_shape` and the feature macros — TMA /
30	WGMMA / fp8 / swizzle — are component-scoped and riskier; they are phase-2 and
31	are **not** emitted by this pass.)
32	
33	> If `_kernel_tuned.json` is absent the build is **byte-identical to before**:
34	> every kernel uses its `#ifndef SG_TUNED_*` default (block 256 / vec 4 /
35	> unroll 1 / async_depth 2; nvcc's own register allocator). A one-line notice
36	> is printed.
37

39	
40	## 0. Prerequisites
41	
42	- A GPU host (the JIT autotuner builds + times real kernels). Steps 1 is
43	  GPU-bound; steps 2–4 only need a CUDA toolchain (`FORCE_CUDA=1` lets the
44	  build configure without a visible device).
45	- `ninja` on PATH (the injection hook patches torch's ninja writer; the build
46	  already requires `use_ninja=True`).
47	- The repo installed editable at least once (so the extension build tree
48	  exists): `FORCE_CUDA=1 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`.

51	
52	## 1. Produce winners → `grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json`
53	
54	Run the JIT autotuner **once per optimizer** (optionally per model). Each run
55	read-merge-writes its winner into the canonical JSON, so 11 sequential runs
56	accumulate 11 entries under the arch key.
57	
58	```bash
59	# One optimizer (sm_90 / Hopper). Repeat for each of the 11.
60	python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \
61	    --optimizer adamw --model decoder --arch sm_90 \
62	    --cache build/.compile_cache.json \
63	    --jit-only --mode bayesian --bayesian-trials 300
64	```
65	
66	Optimizers: `adamw grokadamw grokfast lion looksam muon neuralgrok prodigy
67	supergrok11 supergrok15 supergrok2`. Models (short): `decoder vit mamba`.
68	
69	> **One winner per `(arch, optimizer)` — model is LAST-WINS.** The JSON schema
70	> is `{arch: {optimizer: {...}}}` (no model dimension), so tuning the same
71	> optimizer on a *second* model overwrites the first, and that single winner is
72	> applied to ALL of that optimizer's TUs — its `launch_<opt>.cu` AND every
73	> `mega_<model>_<opt>` megakernel cell across all models. If you tune `decoder`
74	> then `vit` for `adamw`, only `vit`'s `adamw` winner survives. Pick the model
75	> whose launch params you want shipped (the `"model"` field in each entry
76	> records which sweep produced it).
77	
78	A convenience loop:
79	
80	```bash
81	for opt in adamw grokadamw grokfast lion looksam muon \
82	           neuralgrok prodigy supergrok11 supergrok15 supergrok2; do
83	  python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \
84	      --optimizer "$opt" --model decoder --arch sm_90 \
85	      --cache build/.compile_cache.json --jit-only --mode bayesian
86	done
87	```
88	
89	> **Run optimizers SEQUENTIALLY, not in parallel processes.** The exporter's
90	> write is atomic (tmp + `os.replace`), so a reader never sees a half-written
91	> file — but it is read-merge-write, so two concurrent per-optimizer
92	> *processes* can clobber each other's just-written entry. One process at a
93	> time (the loop above) is safe. A failed JSON write is a loud warning in the
94	> compile report and **never** fails the tuning run; the winner is still in the
95	> compile cache and `tuned_configs.h`.
96

101	import pprint;pprint.pprint({k:sorted(v) for k,v in d.items() if k!='_meta'});\

420	    (a wrong eval order would silently drop the base arch/-O3/fast-math flags).

434	    if quote is None:

437	    base = list(base_cuda_post_cflags)
438	    # Map each source's ABSOLUTE object path to its override line. ninja writes
439	    # build edges with os.path.abspath(object), escaping ':' as '$:' and ' '
440	    # as '$ '; we match on the unescaped object path.

447	        full = " ".join(base + [quote(f) for f in flags])
448	        overrides[abs_obj] = f"  cuda_post_cflags = {full}"
449	    if not overrides:

455	    out: List[str] = []

461	            target = parse_ninja_build_target(stripped)
462	            if target is not None and target in overrides:
463	                out.append(overrides[target] + "\n")

471	def parse_ninja_build_target(stmt: str) -> Optional[str]:
472	    """Return the (unescaped) object path from a ninja
473	    ``build <obj>: <rule> <ins>`` statement, or ``None``.
474	
475	    ninja escapes ``:`` as ``$:`` and `` `` as ``$ `` inside paths; we walk
476	    the token, treating ``$<c>`` as a literal pair, and stop at the first
477	    UNescaped ``:`` (the rule separator).
478	    """
479	    if not stmt.startswith("build "):
480	        return None
481	    rest = stmt[len("build "):]
482	    i = 0
483	    obj_chars: List[str] = []
484	    found = False
485	    while i < len(rest):
486	        c = rest[i]
487	        if c == "$" and i + 1 < len(rest):
488	            obj_chars.append(rest[i:i + 2])
489	            i += 2
490	            continue
491	        if c == ":":
492	            found = True
493	            break
494	        obj_chars.append(c)
495	        i += 1
496	    if not found:
497	        return None
498	    token = "".join(obj_chars).strip()
499	    return token.replace("$:", ":").replace("$ ", " ")

"""Pallas/TPU launch glue for AdamW.

Algorithm: csrc/algorithms/adamw.h
Self-contained — inlines the per-tensor AdamW math (formerly imported

from __future__ import annotations

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from typing import Tuple


def launch_adamw_step(
    param: jnp.ndarray,
    exp_avg: jnp.ndarray,
    exp_avg_sq: jnp.ndarray,
    grad: jnp.ndarray,
    lr: float,
    beta1: float,
    beta2: float,
    eps: float,
    wd: float,
    bc1: float,
    bc2: float,
) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray]:
    """Per-tensor AdamW step. Returns new (param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq)."""
    m = beta1 * exp_avg + (1.0 - beta1) * grad
    v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - beta2) * grad * grad
    m_hat = m / bc1
    v_hat = v / bc2
    update = m_hat / (jnp.sqrt(v_hat) + eps)
    new_param = param - lr * (update + wd * param)
    return new_param, m, v


launch_adamw_step_jit = jax.jit(
    launch_adamw_step, static_argnames=("lr", "beta1", "beta2", "eps", "wd")
)

def resolve_macros(config: Dict[str, Any], dim_specs: List[Dict[str, Any]],
                   target: str) -> List[str]:
    """Return the ``-DFOO=VAL`` flags for a config restricted to ``target``."""
    if target not in _VALID_TARGETS:
        raise ValueError(f"target={target!r} not in {_VALID_TARGETS}")
    out: List[str] = []
    for spec in dim_specs:
        macro = spec.get("macro")
        applies_to = spec.get("applies_to", ["host", "device"])

        if not macro:

        name = spec["name"]
        if name not in config:
            continue
        value = config[name]
        # §3.3 nvcc-safe tuple emission. A `-DFOO=a,b,c` flag is rejected by

        # -D lexer splits the value on commas. So for tuple-valued dims (e.g.

        # C++ side reassembles the triplet for __cluster_dims__. We also emit
        # FOO_VOLUME (product) for the host-side fits-in-one-cluster check.

## Per-arch sweep cost (TPE, not grid — build-dominated)

Sweep mechanics: Optuna TPE, optimizers run **sequentially** (runbook §1, read-merge-write race), `--bayesian-trials` ~300–500 or multi-criterion auto-stop (`bayesian_trials=None`). Per-trial cost is **nvcc/hipcc build-dominated** (megakernel cells slowest), plus a short on-device timing.

**Critical framing:** new live dims do **not** multiply the build count — they **dilute the fixed trial budget**, raising trials-to-converge by ~1.5–2×. This is the argument for adding dims sparingly.

- **sm_90**: 2 body archs total in the fleet, but sm_90 is the one with bodies. Adding the NOW dims (#1 MIN_BLOCKS SAFE, #2 reg-split SAFE) is cheap — SAFE dims need no parity re-run. Block-size dims (#3/#6/#7) and grad-tile (#5) each need a **parity-gate re-run** post-sweep. Estimated sweep: 11 opt × ~300–450 trials × (build≈seconds–minutes/cell) ≈ the existing per-opt budget × ~1.5–2 if the RISKY block dims are added; SAFE-only addition is near-free dilution.
- **gfx942**: only #8 (HIP mega block) + #10 (scan minBlocks) are real today; the 4 AMD dead dims stay pinned. Lower trial count (smaller live space). Same sequential 11-opt structure.
- **Pallas/TPU**: **do not add trials** until the kwargs are wired (else pure waste on identical configs).

**Recommended order:** (1) the two **SAFE** NOW rows (#1 `MIN_BLOCKS`, #2 prod/cons regs) — register + ship, no parity re-run, lowest risk/highest certainty. (2) the **RISKY** block/tile/grad rows (#3,5,6,7,8,9,11,12) — each requires the source guard edit (outside this scope) + a `parity_gate_h100.py` re-run after the sweep. (3) **R2 headers** — only after wgmma/tile_pipeline are `#include`d by a real compute TU. (4) **Pallas** — only after `pl.pallas_call` kwarg wiring.
